riskExplain.unclassified: This system has not been classified under the EU AI Act yet.
riskExplain.prohibited: The answers point to a prohibited AI practice (Art. 5). Such a system may not be placed on the market, put into service or used in the EU.
riskExplain.high: A high-risk AI system (Art. 6). It needs risk management, data governance, technical documentation, logging, human oversight, accuracy and robustness, and registration before use.
riskExplain.limited: Limited risk: the transparency duties of Art. 50 apply, such as telling people they are dealing with AI or marking generated content.
riskExplain.minimal: Minimal risk: no specific AI Act duties beyond AI literacy (Art. 4). Voluntary codes of conduct are encouraged (Art. 95).

roleHelp.provider: You develop the AI system (or have it developed) and place it on the market or put it into service under your own name.
roleHelp.deployer: You use an AI system under your authority in your work, for example a tool bought from a vendor.
roleHelp.provider_and_deployer: You build the system and also use it yourselves.
roleHelp.importer: You bring an AI system from a provider outside the EU onto the EU market.
roleHelp.distributor: You make an AI system available on the EU market without being its provider or importer.
roleHelp.not_applicable: The AI Act does not apply, for example purely personal or research use.

kindHelp.classification: Work out the AI Act risk class and the obligations that follow (opens the wizard).
kindHelp.impact: Assess the consequences of the system for individuals, groups and society (ISO/IEC 42001 6.1.4).
kindHelp.fria: Required before a deployer that is a public body, provides public services or does credit scoring or insurance pricing uses a high-risk system (Art. 27).

prohibited.subliminal_manipulation: Subliminal, manipulative or deceptive techniques that distort behaviour and cause significant harm
prohibited.exploiting_vulnerabilities: Exploiting vulnerabilities due to age, disability or social or economic situation
prohibited.social_scoring: Social scoring that leads to detrimental or unfavourable treatment
prohibited.crime_risk_profiling: Predicting the risk of a person committing a crime based only on profiling or personality traits
prohibited.facial_image_scraping: Building facial recognition databases by untargeted scraping of images from the internet or CCTV
prohibited.emotion_recognition_work_education: Emotion recognition in the workplace or in education (except for medical or safety reasons)
prohibited.biometric_categorisation_sensitive: Biometric categorisation to infer race, political opinions, union membership, religion, sex life or sexual orientation
prohibited.realtime_remote_biometric_identification: Real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement

annexIii.critical_infrastructure: Safety components of critical infrastructure (traffic, water, gas, heating, electricity, digital infrastructure)
annexIii.education: Education and vocational training (admission, assessment, monitoring of tests)
annexIii.employment: Employment and workers management (recruitment, promotion, termination, task allocation, monitoring)
annexIii.essential_services: Access to essential private and public services (benefits, credit scoring, life and health insurance pricing, emergency calls)
annexIii.justice_democracy: Administration of justice and democratic processes

transparency.interacts_with_people: It interacts directly with people (for example a chatbot or assistant)
transparency.synthetic_content: It generates synthetic audio, images, video or text
transparency.emotion_or_biometric_categorisation: It recognises emotions or categorises people biometrically
transparency.deep_fake: It creates or manipulates content that is a deep fake
transparency.public_interest_text: It generates or manipulates text published to inform the public on matters of public interest

reasons.high_profiling: The system profiles natural persons, so the Art. 6(3) exception cannot apply ({{ ref }})
reasons.exception_art6_3: Annex III area, but the system only performs a narrow or preparatory task without materially influencing decisions ({{ ref }})
reasons.minimal: None of the prohibited, high-risk or transparency criteria apply ({{ ref }})
reasons.gpai: Built on or is a general-purpose AI model ({{ ref }})
reasons.gpai_systemic: The general-purpose AI model has systemic risk ({{ ref }})

result.exceptionApplied: The Art. 6(3) exception was applied. Document why the system is not high-risk and register it (Art. 6(4)).

obligations.none: No specific obligations for this classification.

role.title: What is your role for this system?
role.body: Obligations depend on whether you provide the system, use it, or bring it to the market.
role.ask: Explain the difference between a provider and a deployer under the EU AI Act, with examples.

prohibited.title: Does the system do any of these prohibited things?
prohibited.body: Article 5 bans a small set of practices outright. Tick any that apply; most systems tick none.
prohibited.ask: Explain the prohibited AI practices in Article 5 of the EU AI Act in plain language.

highRisk.title: Is it a high-risk system?
highRisk.body: A system is high-risk if it is a safety component of a regulated product (Annex I) or used in one of the Annex III areas.
highRisk.ask: Explain when an AI system is high-risk under Article 6 and Annex III of the EU AI Act, and when the Article 6(3) exception applies.

transparency.title: Do people need to be told about the AI?
transparency.body: Article 50 sets transparency duties for systems that interact with people or generate content.
transparency.ask: Explain the transparency obligations in Article 50 of the EU AI Act.

gpai.title: General-purpose AI models
gpai.body: Providers of general-purpose AI models have their own duties (Art. 53, and Art. 55 for systemic risk).
gpai.ask: Explain what a general-purpose AI model is under the EU AI Act and what its providers must do.

deployer.title: Deployer situation
deployer.body: Some deployers of high-risk systems must carry out a fundamental rights impact assessment (Art. 27).
deployer.ask: Explain when a deployer must carry out a fundamental rights impact assessment under Article 27 of the EU AI Act.

q.annexI: It is a safety component of a product (or is itself a product) covered by EU harmonisation legislation in Annex I, such as machinery, toys, lifts, medical devices or vehicles
q.annexIii: It is used in one of these areas (Annex III):
q.exception: It only performs a narrow procedural or preparatory task, improves the result of a human activity, or detects patterns without replacing human assessment (Art. 6(3))
q.gpai: It is (or we provide) a general-purpose AI model
q.gpaiSystemic: The model has systemic risk (high-impact capabilities, Art. 51)
q.publicService: We are a public body or a private body providing public services
q.creditInsurance: We use it for creditworthiness or credit scoring, or for risk assessment and pricing of life or health insurance

answers.annexI: Safety component of an Annex I product
answers.gpaiSystemic: General-purpose AI model with systemic risk
answers.creditInsurance: Credit scoring or life / health insurance pricing

intended_use.title: Intended use and context
intended_use.hint: What the system is for, who uses it, in which processes and decisions.

affected_parties.title: Affected individuals and groups
affected_parties.hint: Who is affected by its outputs, including vulnerable groups and people who do not use it themselves.

foreseeable_misuse.title: Reasonably foreseeable misuse
foreseeable_misuse.hint: How the system could be used in ways it was not meant for, and what that would cause.

impacts_individuals.title: Impacts on individuals
impacts_individuals.hint: Possible effects on safety, privacy, fairness, autonomy and other rights of individuals.

impacts_society.title: Impacts on society
impacts_society.hint: Wider effects, for example on the environment, employment, democracy or public trust.

mitigations.title: Measures to reduce the impacts
mitigations.hint: Controls, human oversight, design changes and communication that reduce the impacts.

residual_impact.title: Remaining impact
residual_impact.hint: What is left after the measures, and why it is acceptable.

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.hint: Your overall judgement and any conditions for use.

process_description.title: (a) Processes in which the system is used
process_description.hint: Describe the deployer's processes in which the high-risk system will be used, in line with its intended purpose.

period_and_frequency.title: (b) Period and frequency of use
period_and_frequency.hint: How long and how often each high-risk AI system is intended to be used.

affected_categories.title: (c) Categories of persons affected
affected_categories.hint: The categories of natural persons and groups likely to be affected in this context.

specific_risks.title: (d) Specific risks of harm
specific_risks.hint: The specific risks of harm to those categories, taking into account the provider's information (Art. 13).

human_oversight_measures.title: (e) Human oversight measures
human_oversight_measures.hint: How human oversight is carried out, following the instructions for use.

mitigation_and_complaints.title: (f) Measures if risks materialise
mitigation_and_complaints.hint: What is done if the risks materialise, including internal governance and complaint mechanisms.

docs.title: Documentation: {{ name }}
docs.requiredBody: This is a high-risk system: the technical documentation in Annex IV must be drawn up before it is placed on the market or put into service, and kept up to date (Art. 11).
docs.optionalBody: Annex IV is only mandatory for high-risk systems, but writing these sections is good practice under ISO/IEC 42001 and helps if the classification changes.
docs.completeness: Annex IV: {{ done }} of {{ total }} sections written
docs.ask: Help me write the "{{ section }}" documentation section for this AI system.

data_documentation.title: Data documentation
data_documentation.hint: Where the data comes from, how it was collected and prepared, quality checks, and known gaps or biases.

model_documentation.title: Model documentation
model_documentation.hint: The models used, their versions, providers, how they were chosen and their known limitations.

human_oversight.title: Human oversight design
human_oversight.hint: Who oversees the system, how they can understand, override or stop it, and how automation bias is avoided.

logging.title: Logging
logging.hint: What the system records automatically, how long logs are kept and who can read them.

accuracy_robustness.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
accuracy_robustness.hint: Expected accuracy and how it is measured, resilience to errors and attacks.

post_market_plan.title: Post-market monitoring plan
post_market_plan.hint: How performance and incidents are followed up once the system is in use, and how often it is reviewed.

general_description.title: 1. General description
general_description.hint: Intended purpose, provider, version, how it interacts with other systems, hardware and the instructions for use.

development_process.title: 2. Development process and design
development_process.hint: Design choices, system architecture, data requirements, human oversight measures, validation and testing.

monitoring_and_control.title: 3. Monitoring, functioning and control
monitoring_and_control.hint: Capabilities and limitations, foreseeable unintended outcomes, oversight measures and input data specifications.

performance_metrics.title: 4. Performance metrics
performance_metrics.hint: Why the chosen metrics are appropriate for this system.

risk_management.title: 5. Risk management system
risk_management.hint: The risk management system under Art. 9.

lifecycle_changes.title: 6. Changes over the lifecycle
lifecycle_changes.hint: Relevant changes made by the provider through the system's lifecycle.

harmonised_standards.title: 7. Standards applied
harmonised_standards.hint: Harmonised standards or other specifications applied, and solutions used where none apply.

declaration_of_conformity.title: 8. EU declaration of conformity
declaration_of_conformity.hint: A copy of the EU declaration of conformity (Art. 47).

post_market_evaluation.title: 9. Post-market performance evaluation
post_market_evaluation.hint: The system for evaluating performance after placing on the market, including the post-market monitoring plan (Art. 72).
